titulo: Müssen, wollen e dürfen: obligation, will and permission: Müssen: to have to

aula.titulo: Müssen, wollen e dürfen: obligation, will and permission
aula.objetivo: Use «müssen» (must / have to), «wollen» (to want) and «dürfen» (to be allowed to) and read the most common signs, always with the sentence frame.

blocos.titulo: Müssen: obligation and necessity, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: «müssen» expresses what you HAVE TO do (obligation or necessity): «Ich muss arbeiten» = I have to work. STEP 2: conjugate: ich muss, du musst, er muss, wir müssen, ihr müsst, sie müssen. The «ü» disappears in the singular and, as with «können», «ich» and «er» are the same, with no -t. STEP 3: the second verb goes to the END, in the infinitive: «Du musst pünktlich sein.» STEP 4: question: «Muss ich heute arbeiten?» STEP 5: with a separable verb, it stays WHOLE at the end: «Ich muss um sieben Uhr aufstehen.» In English we say «have to» or «must»; in German there is no verb «have» here: the modal does everything on its own.
blocos.comparacao: English says «have to» (the verb have + to) or «must». German has a verb of its own, «müssen», which is conjugated and leaves the other verb in the infinitive, at the end.

erros.motivo: In the «er» form, no -st and no -t.

erros.errado: Ich muss aufstehe um sieben Uhr.
erros.certo: Ich muss um sieben Uhr aufstehen.
erros.motivo: The whole infinitive goes to the end.

blocos.enunciado: Say 5 things you have to do today: «Ich muss …»
Write the 6 forms of «können» and one sentence with each.
